attrs.evidence: probe_semoracle_v10_repro.mjs, paired and gating: 2/2 reproduce against a frozen v0.9.0 acceptance — P-4, where an issued request for const(5) is accepted as 999 because the caller passed {verify: () => ({ok:true}), get: () => ({op:'const',value:999})} and the identical result is refused as foreign-result-divergence by the real registry; and P-4b, where the oracle is a GENUINE ProgramRegistry instance holding a different program, which is the case an instanceof check cannot see. 5/5 confined live: no registry parameter on execute or accept, a registry severed at construction so editing the caller's AST afterwards changes nothing, bindProgram unable to repoint an issued id, the whole four-rung surface checked as a set, and the World reader confirmed inert as a parameter too. derive_realm_battery.mjs 20/20 (case 18: an authority constructed holding no programs answers program-unknown from the far side), derive_battery.mjs 45/45.
attrs.statement: AN AUTHORITY CANNOT VALIDATE A SEMANTIC CLAIM USING A PROGRAM RESOLVER SUPPLIED BY THE CLAIMANT. Acceptance takes no proof from its caller — INCLUDING the mapping from semantic identity to semantic program. Re-derivation is only evidence if the authority chose what it re-derived against. The supplier ladder this closes has four rungs and one shape: @1 the caller supplied the implementation LABEL (deriveLocally's third parameter), @2 the registration NAME (registerExecutor), @3 the ACTION beside the artifact evidence (a launcher's spawn), @4 the SEMANTIC ORACLE at acceptance (accept's registry parameter). Any field a caller controls on the path to a verdict becomes the verdict. AN instanceof CHECK DOES NOT CLOSE IT, and a law that read as 'check the type' would invite exactly the wrong repair: a Proxy satisfies the type, and so does a genuine ProgramRegistry the caller populated with a different program. The repair is OWNERSHIP. The registry is BUILT at the authority's construction from canonical program DATA — ProgramRegistry.bind severs it through canonicalBytes — so the authority owns its semantic oracle rather than sharing an object with whoever built it, and no registry parameter crosses execute() or accept() again. bindProgram remains an explicit authority operation and needs no second rule, because ids are content-bound: teaching the authority const(999) gives it a new id and cannot repoint const(5)'s. So every oracle the authority consults is constructor-time — the World reader (round 17), the semantic registry (here), and the execution host with its immutable catalog (derivation.implementation-provenance@4) — and what a caller supplies is an INTENT and a RESULT TO VALIDATE.
